# Priya Nair

Engineering lead @ Northstar Robotics. Joined year 2 (so ~2023), came from a bigger robotics
company where she was tired of shipping demos that never survived contact with a real warehouse
floor.

Owns: routing engine, fleet coordinator, and firmware (the last one somewhat unwillingly — quote
from a design review: "I did not sign up to debug motor controllers but here we are").

She's the one behind the "boring reliability" engineering philosophy that basically everyone at the
company repeats now — rohan gets credit for saying it publicly first but priya's the one who
actually enforces it in code review. Her rule of thumb: if a failure mode isn't boring (i.e., it
doesn't fail into a safe, obvious, loggable stop-state), it doesn't ship.

Runs the tuesday live standup (everything else is async). Not a fan of long meetings — the standup
notes from her runs tend to be shorter than everyone else's.

Random: she has a running feud with the office thermostat, nobody knows why but its mentioned in
like 3 different slack threads.
